function: Learns V2V channel selection, V2V transmit power and discrete RIS phase shifts at the BS to minimize V2I age of information and raise V2V payload delivery (pp. 5-6).
system: Single-antenna vehicles, BS with M=4-element ULA, uplink; passive reflecting RIS, F=12 elements, Q=8 discrete phases; 2 GHz carrier, 1 MHz bandwidth (pp. 3, 5, 9).
method: Soft Actor-Critic deep reinforcement learning, one central agent at the BS; fully connected actor and critics, three hidden layers of 512 neurons; 1000 training episodes (pp. 6, 8).
data_channel: No dataset; custom simulator: V2I path loss 128.1+37.6log10(d), V2V WINNER+ B1 Manhattan LOS, Rayleigh fast fading, own RIS channel model (p. 4, Table I p. 9).
test_conditions: 1000 training episodes; tests of 50 slots averaged over 10 runs, sweeping V2I power 13-23 dBm, payload size, RIS elements 10-120, users 4-12 (pp. 8-10).
baselines: Non-learned: Random RIS Random RA, NO RIS Random RA. Learned: PPO, TD3, DDPG, each controlling spectrum, power and RIS phase shifts (p. 8).
metrics: Reward, V2V payload success probability, sum V2I rate, sum V2I AoI, average rate per user, versus V2I power, payload size, RIS elements and users (pp. 8-11).
complexity: Big-O training complexity O((E·S−I)(GE+GA+2GC+UE+UA+4UC)) in symbolic gradient and update costs; no runtime or parameter count (p. 8).
openness: Source code released at https://github.com/qiongwu86/RISRB-AoI-V2X-DRL.git (p. 3); no dataset, data are simulated.
q1_support: p. 8: "We construct the vehicular environment according to [58], [59] and [60]" (3GPP TS 22.186, TR 36.885, WINNER II); p. 4: "small-scale fading power component, which is assumed to be exponentially distributed with unit mean". Own simulator with path loss, shadowing and Rayleigh values and own RIS link model; no listed standard model or measured data.
q2_support: p. 8: "we conduct tests based on the training model", with one default setting. The V2I power, payload, RIS element and user sweeps (pp. 9-11) are not said to reuse a trained model; F and the user count change the state and action size (p. 6).
q3_support: p. 8: "use three different algorithms, PPO, TD3, and DDPG to control the spectrum and power of the vehicle" (learned) and "the resource allocation of the vehicle to be random" (non-learned random RIS and allocation); p. 9: "improved by 33.2% compared to DDPG"; Figs. 5-8 compare success rate, V2I rate and AoI.
q4_support: p. 8: "the complexity of our approach in the training stage is O((E · S − I)(GE + GA + 2GC + UE + UA + 4UC ))" in Section III-C, Computational Complexity Analysis. It is symbolic and covers training only; no FLOPs or runtime.
q5_support: p. 3: "The source code has been released at: https://github.com/qiongwu86/RISRB-AoI-V2X-DRL.git"
notes: Included under the joint rule: the SAC policy sets RIS phase shifts and V2V power together with the channel assignment (p. 6, Eq. 16), so area 3 for the RIS configuration. q1 borderline: only path loss, shadowing and Rayleigh fading values follow TR 36.885 and WINNER II (Table I, p. 9; refs. [59], [60]) and the V2V channel is taken from ref. [39] (p. 4), so not met; reviewer to confirm. q2: no train-test mismatch is stated. q4 rests on the symbolic training complexity of Section III-C.
